questions.text:
The product of all eigenvalues of the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix}
1 & 2 & 3\\ 
4 & 5 &6 \\ 
7 &8  & 9
\end{bmatrix}[/latex] is
questions.solution:
Product of all eigenvalues [latex]=\det(A)[/latex].

[latex]\det(A)=1(45-48)-2(36-42)+3(32-35)=-3+12-9=0[/latex]

(Quick check: [latex]R_1+R_3=2R_2[/latex], so the rows are dependent and the matrix is singular.)

Answer: 0

questions.text: The value of the definite integral [latex] \int_{-3}^{3}  \int_{-2}^{2}  \int_{-1}^{1} (4x^2y-z^3)dzdydx[/latex] is _____. (Rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Split the integrand:
- [latex]4x^2y[/latex]: odd in y, integrated over the symmetric range [latex][-2,2][/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0
- [latex]z^3[/latex]: odd in z, integrated over [latex][-1,1][/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0

Total = 0

Answer: 0

questions.text:
Let A be the adjacency matrix of the graph with vertices {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.

Let [latex]\lambda _1,\lambda _2,\lambda _3,\lambda _4,\; and \; \lambda _5[/latex] be the five eigenvalues of A. Note that these eigenvalues need not be distinct.
The value of [latex]\lambda _1+\lambda _2+\lambda _3+ \lambda _4+ \lambda _5 =[/latex] _____
questions.solution:
Sum of eigenvalues = trace of A = sum of the diagonal entries.

A diagonal entry [latex]a_{ii}[/latex] is 1 only if vertex i has a self-loop. In the graph, vertices 3 and 4 have self-loops, so trace [latex]=1+1=2[/latex].

Answer: 2

questions.text:
Let [latex]f(x)=x^3+15x^2-33x-36 [/latex] be a real-valued function.
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
[latex]f'(x)=3x^2+30x-33=3(x^2+10x-11)=3(x+11)(x-1)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] critical points [latex]x=-11[/latex] and [latex]x=1[/latex].

[latex]f''(x)=6x+30[/latex]:
- [latex]f''(-11)=-36 \lt 0[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] local maximum
- [latex]f''(1)=36 \gt 0[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] local minimum

Answer: f(x) has a local maximum and has a local minimum

questions.text:
Let [latex] A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 &4 \\ 4& 1& 2 &3 \\ 3& 4 & 1 &2 \\ 2 &3 &4 &1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] and [latex] B=\begin{bmatrix} 3& 4 & 1 &2 \\ 4& 1& 2 &3 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 &4 \\ 2 &3 &4 &1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
Let det(A) and det(B) denote the determinants of the matrices A and B, respectively.
Which one of the options given below is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Rows of B are rows of A in the order [latex]R_3,R_2,R_1,R_4[/latex], i.e. B is A with rows 1 and 3 swapped.

One row swap changes the sign of the determinant: [latex]\det(B)=-\det(A)[/latex].

Answer: det(B) = [latex]-[/latex]det(A)
